paragraphs: Swamiji shared an old Hindu legend in which the Lord was once born on earth as a pig. He found a pig for a mate, and in time a litter of little piglets arrived. He was perfectly content with his family, rolling about in the mud and squealing happily, having completely forgotten His divine glory.

The gods were alarmed. They came down to earth and pleaded with Him to leave the pig's body and return to heaven. He refused flat out and chased them away. He was very happy, He told them, and wanted to be left alone.
With no other option, the gods destroyed the pig body. Instantly the Lord's divine majesty came back to Him, and He was amazed that He could ever have found any joy in being a pig.

Swamiji said we behave just like this. When people hear about the Impersonal God, the infinite Self, they panic: what will happen to my individuality? I will lose myself! Next time that fear comes up, he said, remember the pig. Each of us holds an endless mine of happiness, yet we cling to our present little condition. Once you realise what you truly are, you will be astonished you ever hesitated to let go of a life ruled by the senses. Is our little personality really any better than that pig life?
learn: We often hold on tightly to small comforts and habits because they are familiar, even when something far better is waiting. When you resist growth because you fear losing who you are, ask whether you are really just clinging to the mud.
